description: NASA Space Apps Challenge kapsamında yenilikçi bir projeye katkı sağlamak ve uzay/havacılık teknolojilerine yazılım perspektifinden yaklaşmak amacıyla bu yarışmada yer almak istiyoruz. Yazılım geliştirme, sistem optimizasyonu ve veri yönetimi konularına duyduğumuz yoğun ilgi sayesinde, projelerin teknik altyapısında ve problem çözme süreçlerinde aktif rol alabiliyoruz.
summary:
MAYDUSS – Astronaut Health Monitoring System

MAYDUSS is a web-based astronaut health monitoring and management system designed to simulate how wearable devices could help monitor astronauts during space missions. The program displays important health indicators, including heart rate, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), and suit pressure. It includes an alert system that warns users when simulated measurements fall outside predefined limits.

MAYDUSS has a login system with separate astronaut and administrator accounts. Each astronaut can view their own health data, while the administrator has access to all astronaut profiles, system records, and management features. The interface allows the administrator to switch between astronauts and manage their information.

This project addresses the challenge of organizing astronaut health information and identifying potentially abnormal readings quickly. It is important because continuous health monitoring and timely alerts can support astronaut safety during missions. Currently, MAYDUSS uses simulated data and does not connect to real wearable sensors, but it demonstrates the basic concepts of a future monitoring system.
details:
MAYDUSS – Astronaut Health Monitoring and Management System

What does the project do and how does it work?

MAYDUSS is a web-based prototype designed to simulate an astronaut health monitoring system inspired by wearable devices. It displays three main measurements: heart rate (BPM), blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), and spacesuit pressure. The values update during the simulation, and an alert system warns the user when a measurement goes outside predefined thresholds.

The application includes two types of accounts. Astronauts can log in to view their own health information, while the administrator can access the overall dashboard, switch between astronaut profiles, manage astronaut information, and review system events. This role-based design demonstrates how health information could be organized for individual astronauts and mission personnel.

What are its benefits and intended impact?

MAYDUSS demonstrates how health indicators and automated alerts could help mission personnel notice unusual measurements more quickly. Its main goal is to explore how a clear interface could make astronaut health information easier to monitor and understand. In future versions, the system could be expanded to receive data from compatible wearable sensors, store historical measurements, and support more advanced trend analysis. These improvements could contribute to astronaut safety and more informed monitoring during space missions.

What tools and technologies were used?

The prototype was developed as a browser-based application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML structures the interface, CSS provides the visual design, and JavaScript controls interactions, simulated measurements, account selection, and alert behavior. The application runs in a web browser and does not currently require dedicated hardware. No physical wearable sensors or real astronaut health data are connected.

What makes the project creative?

MAYDUSS combines simulated wearable-device measurements, automatic alerts, individual astronaut views, and an administrator dashboard in one interface. Instead of displaying health values alone, it demonstrates how different users could interact with the same monitoring system according to their roles.

What factors did the team consider?

The project considered ease of use, clear presentation of measurements, quick identification of unusual readings, separation of astronaut and administrator views, and the importance of protecting personal health information. The prototype also acknowledges that simulated values cannot replace real sensor measurements or professional medical assessment. Future development would require secure authentication, reliable hardware integration, validated alert thresholds, and appropriate data protection.

Current status: MAYDUSS is an educational prototype. Its measurements are simulated, and its alerts demonstrate a concept rather than provide validated medical or spaceflight safety warnings.
